newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE euroyen flat after late recovery in stocks.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE euroyen flat after late recovery in stocks.

text.p: The key March three-month euroyen interest rate futures contract settled unchanged on Wednesday after giving up earlier gains as the Nikkei-225 stock average recovered to positive territory towards the close.

When the Nikkei fell below 20,000 in the morning, the contract rose to match a key resistance of 98.95. Domestic banks then bought fixed interest rates in the interest rate swap (IRS) market, also prompting buying in euroyen futures.

But further buying of the March contract was curbed as current price levels suggest that the market has factored in its expectation that there will be no change in the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) monetary policy by the year-end, traders said.
A BOJ rate rise is still possible depending on the economic recovery later this year, they said.
"We needed something new to continue to buy. The weakness in Tokyo stocks was not enough for the March to rise above 98.95," said a long-term bank dealer.
The March was at 98.92 after moving between 98.91 and 98.95. Turnover was 59,517 contracts.

Traders said there is an upperside target at 98.98, a recent high before the stronger-than-expected results of the BOJ's "tankan" corporate sentiment survey resulted in a correction in the market's too pessimistic view of the economy.

In the cash market, the key three-month certificates of deposit (CD) rate eased to 0.68 percent from Tuesday's 11-month high of 0.70 percent after the BOJ conducted an unusually accommodative operation for the second day in a row.
Given the bank's consistently generous operation, which left the market with a surplus of some 400 billion yen, the key overnight rate also fell to 0.47 percent from Tuesday's 0.48.

About 110 billion yen worth of the three-month CDs were issued at 0.68 percent after the CDs were issued at 0.69 percent in the morning. The rate of the three-month CDs maturing after end-September, marking the fiscal half year, is usually higher than those with shorter-term maturities.
Some 30 billion yen of one-month CDs were issued at 0.60 percent, down from the previously issued rate of 0.61. But two-month CDs were offered only at 0.61 percent, traders said.
Three-year IRS rates were quoted at 1.46/1.50 percent at 0718 GMT, down from Tuesday's 1.48/1.52 percent.
